turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - cdft_topo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties
    are NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the
    crystal structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal chemistry,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, select the 5
candidates with the LARGEST spin-orbit spillage that also satisfy a bulk-gap
requirement: the band gap must be at least 1 eV. Band gaps are NOT given for
the pool -- you must infer them. A selected candidate whose band gap is
below the threshold scores zero.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The pool is dominated by intermetallics, Heuslers and other close-packed phases whose electron counts and bonding are incompatible with a bulk gap. Only a minority of candidates are closed-shell (or unambiguously semiconducting) and therefore able to satisfy \(E_g\ge 1\,\mathrm{eV}\).

Among those gapped phases the spin-orbit spillage scales with the atomic number of the heaviest element that contributes to the frontier orbitals. This immediately ranks the viable insulators as

- BiTe\(_2\)Br\(_4\) (Bi \(Z=83\)),
- In\(_2\)HgO\(_4\) (Hg \(Z=80\)),
- PtS\(_2\) (Pt \(Z=78\)),
- Ba\(_2\)CaWO\(_6\) (W \(Z=74\)),
- PdI\(_2\) (I \(Z=53\)).

All five are electronically closed-shell (or known semiconductors) with gaps well above the 1 eV threshold; all other high-\(Z\) formulae in the pool are metals or have \(E_g<1\,\mathrm{eV}\) and therefore score zero.

Final: c048, c034, c022, c049, c097
